public_rationale: The May 16, 2023 hearing included competing approaches, including licensing and a new agency versus reliance on existing regulators [e1]. NIST's November 20, 2024 announcement documents an international safety-institute network and joint testing, showing some concrete cooperation [e3]. The June 4, 2025 CRS report says the federal laws it reviewed established no broad AI regulatory authority, but its observation is later than the May 16 cutoff [e2]. These records do not establish what proportion of the hearing's distinct proposals was operating by May 16, 2025, so they cannot settle 'almost none' [e1–e3].
limitations: The packet lacks a complete proposal-by-proposal implementation inventory through May 16, 2025.
International cooperation and testing do not establish mandatory licensing or an international regulator.
The result may depend on how proposals are grouped and partial or voluntary implementation is counted.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Almost none of the AI regulation discussed at the May 2023 Senate hearing has been implemented as of May 2025.

statement.excerpt: Tragically, almost none of what was discussed that day has come to fruition.
statement.document_title: Two Years Ago Today in AI History: The Tale of An About-face in AI Regulation

our_interpretation: The comparison runs from the May 16, 2023 hearing to publication on May 16, 2025.
The surrounding discussion makes US federal regulation and international governance involving the US the principal scope.
The ordinary reading is that only a small minority of the substantive regulatory proposals had been implemented. It does not mean literally no action.
Implementation requires an operating measure. Introducing legislation or announcing intentions does not suffice. Voluntary cooperation is distinguished from mandatory regulation.
criteria.support_condition: A proposal-by-proposal comparison shows that nearly all substantive regulatory proposals remained unimplemented by May 16, 2025.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The comparison shows substantial implementation across the hearing's substantive regulatory proposals, rather than isolated measures.
